content.thinking:
I'm checking the root-cause claim: the new revision changed the summary cache entries from a bare cents figure to "amount/items" text, which the document's first source supports. The part I'm still testing is whether replicas on the older revision would raise on that text rather than treat it as a miss.

I'm checking whether the older replicas actually raise on the new text. The new reader returns None on a ValueError, so the error has to come from the old reader, and the file path in the message points to the same summary cache module.

I'm checking whether the older replicas' error on the new-format entries really counts as the cause, and whether the rollout's current paused state has any halt or revert behind it. The notes show the rollout stopped partway with both revisions still serving, but nothing yet says what stopped it.

I'm checking the rest of the claims against the record: the missing-check and no-automatic-halt points hold, nobody was paged, and the partial fix was not kept.

supported.quote: The new revision changed what a summary cache entry holds. It used to be a bare cents figure and is now 'amount/items' text (`_ENTRY_FORMAT`).

The replicas still running the earlier revision read those same entries and raised ValueError on the new text in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py instead of treating it as a miss, so the account page request failed.

A software update changed the format of a saved summary of each shopper's spending, and the older version, still running beside the new one because the update stopped partway, could not read the new format and failed the account page.
Account pages could fail again if revision 696c33a goes out again while the earlier revision is still serving, or if cache entries in its new format are left where the earlier revision reads.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose well above its usual level.
The failing account page requests raised ValueError when they read a summary cache entry, '{G3714.1}', that was not a figure in cents, in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py.
The cache held entries in the new 'amount/items' text format that revision 696c33a introduced, and the replicas reading them expected a bare cents figure.
The new revision's own reader returns no error on text it cannot read, so the error comes from the reader in the earlier revision.
Deploy P2 at {P2.1} rolled out revision 696c33a, which brought in the new entry format.
As of {T10.1}, its rolling update was paused partway, with replicas on 696c33a and on 5470c1a both serving against the same cache.

The earlier deploy P1 of revision 5470c1a: the service was measured healthy with it in place. The metrics read before the onset showed the usual error rate, account pages rendered normally before the onset, and the service returned to normal after the confirmed rollback left 5470c1a running.

The new revision changed the format of cache entries that the still-serving older replicas also read, and the older revision's reader raised an error on the new format instead of treating it as a miss.
No check was seen, before the change went out, that the revision already serving could read cache entries in the new revision's format.
No automatic rollout analysis was seen that halted or reverted io-shop's rolling update when its error rate rose. The rollout stayed partway, with both revisions serving.
The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: Code-Fix wrote a fix and said plainly that it helps only together with a change outside the repository, so no partial fix was kept.
